commands.review_summary:
The PR changes AcpClient to spawn non-Windows agent bridges detached, signal their process group on close, and adds a mock-agent regression test for a long-lived grandchild.

Reproducibility: yes. source inspection gives a high-confidence reproduction shape: current main only sends child.kill to the bridge PID, so a bridge-spawned child is not signaled. I did not run a live repro in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Human review is needed because the PR has a process-lifecycle correctness blocker plus a contributor real-behavior-proof gate that automation cannot supply.

target.title: fix(client): reap the bridge process tree on close
target.body:
## Problem

When acpx terminates an agent bridge, `killAgentIfRunning` (`src/acp/client.ts`) calls `child.kill(signal)` — it signals **only the bridge PID**. But the bridge (codex-acp etc.) spawns its own children: the model process and MCP servers (e.g. `serena`). Those grandchildren are never signalled, so they **survive as orphans** and accumulate across runs until the agent app-server chokes and new sessions hang at `session/new`.

## Fix

Spawn the bridge in its **own process group** (`detached: true` on Unix, threaded through `buildSpawnCommandOptions`) so it leads a group whose `pgid == pid`, and on close signal the **whole group** with a negative PID (`process.kill(-pid, signal)`).

The group signal is gated on an `agentGroupLeader` flag that is only set when the child was actually spawned detached — acpx must **never** `process.kill(-pid)` a non-leader, which could hit its own process group (self-kill). Windows and any non-detached path keep the previous single-process `child.kill(signal)`, and a `catch` falls back to it.

The existing `SIGTERM → SIGKILL` escalation is unchanged: group-`SIGTERM` reaps well-behaved descendants, group-`SIGKILL` reaps a stubborn bridge that ignores `SIGTERM`.

## Scope / limitation

This reaps descendants that share the bridge's process group. A grandchild that **re-detaches into its own session** escapes the group signal — inherent to any group-based reaping. Still strictly better than the previous PID-only kill.

This change is orthogonal to abrupt parent death (`SIGKILL`/OOM of acpx itself), which orphaned the bridge both before and after this change (no `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`); a follow-up can address that separately.

## Test

Real-process regression test (Unix-only): the mock agent forks a long-lived grandchild that ignores `SIGTERM` and records its PID; the test drives `AcpClient.start()` then `close()` and asserts the grandchild PID is **dead**. Red before the fix (grandchild survives), green after. Full suite stays green (846 pass, 3 skipped).

---

Maintainer edits enabled (personal fork). Happy to narrow or adjust the approach.
